title: 5.3.13 Your Turn — Build a Sprite
description: Low-stakes autograded practice. Instantiate the Sprite class twice (rectangle form and circle form), set properties on each instance, and give one sprite a stroke. Bridges the 2.2.4 / 2.2.5 worked examples and the 2.2.8 Enemy class lab.

steps.title: Create the canvas
steps.instructions: In `setup()`, create a canvas. `Canvas` is a class, and `new Canvas(...)` stamps out an instance — the same constructor-call pattern you saw in 2.2.4.
hints: Open the shplay docs drawer on the right and find the Canvas section.

steps.title: Instantiate a rectangle sprite
steps.instructions: Store a new rectangle sprite in a variable, using the 4-argument constructor form `new Sprite(x, y, width, height)`. Then set its `.color`.
hints: Check the Sprite section of the shplay docs drawer for the 4-argument constructor form.

steps.title: Instantiate a circle sprite
steps.instructions: Store a second sprite using the 3-argument constructor form `new Sprite(x, y, diameter)`. Give this instance its own `.color` (different from the first, so you can tell them apart).
hints: Check the Sprite section of the shplay docs drawer for the 3-argument constructor form.

steps.title: Give one sprite a stroke
steps.instructions: Pick either sprite and set its `.stroke` AND its `.strokeWeight`. You'll see a visible outline on that sprite.
hints: Look up sprite properties in the shplay docs drawer.

requirements.title: Rectangle sprite (4-arg form)
requirements.description: At least one `new Sprite(x, y, w, h)` call with four arguments.

requirements.title: Circle sprite (3-arg form)
requirements.description: At least one `new Sprite(x, y, diameter)` call with exactly three arguments.

requirements.title: Property set on an instance
requirements.description: At least one `.color` assignment on a sprite instance.
